memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the eighth day they must bring them for their cleansing to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting, before the LORD. The priest is to take the lamb for the guilt offering, together with the log of oil, and wave them before the LORD as a wave offering. He shall slaughter the lamb for the guilt offering and take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot." - Lev 14:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice what has not changed. The poor person still comes on the eighth day. Still to the entrance of the tent of meeting. Still before the LORD. And still the blood goes on the ear, the thumb, the toe.

The offering was smaller. The ceremony is not. Nobody hurried this person through a shortened version because they were poor. They received the full, unhurried attention of the priest — the same words, the same actions, the same dignity.

That should shape us. It is remarkably easy for churches to give their best attention to the people who can give the most, and a quicker, thinner welcome to those who cannot. James saw it happening in the first century and named it plainly — the man with the gold ring gets the good seat, the poor man is left standing (Jas 2:2-4). It has never stopped happening.

But God is no respecter of persons. God does not show favouritism (Acts 10:34). The same blood, the same places, the same care.

If you have ever felt like a lesser member of God's family — less educated, less wealthy, less impressive — read verse 25 again. Ear, thumb, toe. Exactly the same as everyone else.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat people differently based on what they can offer you?
2. Have you ever felt like a second-class member of God's family?
3. What would a truly impartial welcome look like in your church?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You show no favouritism and give the same care to all. Search my heart for partiality, and make me someone who welcomes as You welcome. Amen.
